added.title: Research Associate in Mathematical and Computational Foundations of Reservoir Computing
added.description:
Description

Role:
Research Associate in Mathematical and Computational Foundations of Reservoir Computing

Grade and Salary:
Grade 7 - £38,448 to £46,970 per annum

FTE and working pattern:
1 FTE (full-time – 35 hours per week) fixed term for 24 months

Holiday Entitlement:
33 days annual leave plus 9 buildings-closed days (and Christmas Eve when it falls on a weekday). Use our total rewards calculator:  https://www.hw.ac.uk/about/work/total-rewards-calculator.htm to see the value of benefits provided by Heriot-Watt University

Purpose of Role

We are recruiting a 24-month, full-time research associate to contribute to the UKRI-funded project “Taking Material Reservoir Computers FARR: Foundations for Adaptation, Resilience and Recovery.”

Our vision is to develop theoretical and computational foundations for a new generation of adaptable, resilient, and recoverable computing systems. The project brings together researchers from Heriot-Watt, Oxford, Liverpool, Sussex, and Ulster universities to investigate reservoir computing, with a particular focus on its potential for low-power, real-time decision making in challenging environments.

You will undertake original research at the intersection of applied mathematics, statistics, and optimisation to better understand how reservoir computers process and retain information. Your research will focus on characterising the behaviour of reservoir computers, investigating the role of memory in decision-making, and developing methods to quantify uncertainty. You will also develop and evaluate computational approaches that enable reservoir computers to adapt to changing conditions and recover from disruption.

The successful candidate will be based in the School of Mathematical and Computer Sciences at Heriot-Watt University. You will work closely with an interdisciplinary team of researchers across the five partner institutions.

This work is being undertaken in cooperation with UK Government stakeholders. The successful candidate will be required to obtain security clearance before taking up the post, and must be eligible for UK security clearance in principle, e.g., by nationality (British Citizen) or 5+ years UK residency etc. Eligibility criteria and further information on the process can be found on the UK Government security vetting website, see https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels/national-security-vetting-clearance-levels.

Anticipated start date: January 2027, or a later date by mutual agreement.

Candidates can make informal enquiries about this position to Eric Hall E.Hall@hw.ac.uk OR Michael Lones M.Lones@hw.ac.uk.

Key Duties & Responsibilities

Conduct and disseminate original research aligned with the project, in collaboration with the wider team.
Develop mathematical and statistical methods to characterise reservoir computing systems, with a particular focus on memory, decision-making, and uncertainty quantification.
Develop, implement, and evaluate computational methods to investigate the adaptation, resilience, and recovery of reservoir computing systems.
Work closely with the supervisory team to develop and plan research objectives.
Prepare research reports and contribute to publications in peer-reviewed journals and conference proceedings.
Present research findings and contribute to technical workshops, seminars, and conferences, as appropriate.
Undertake training and professional development activities, as necessary and agreed with the supervisory team, to support project objectives and further career development.
Undertake any other duties commensurate with the grade of the post.

Essential

Essential & Desirable Criteria

PhD in mathematical sciences, computer science, or a closely related discipline, or currently working towards the completion of such a PhD.
Experience of mathematical modelling, statistical analysis, or optimisation.
Experience in scientific programming and computational research, using languages such as Python, MATLAB, or Julia.
Experience of, or willingness to work with, researchers from other disciplines.
Evidence of self-motivation and the ability to work independently.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Excellent time management and organisational skills, including the ability to prioritise workload.

Desirable

Experience in stochastic processes, dynamical systems, or time-series analysis.
Experience or knowledge of uncertainty quantification, statistical inference, or information-theoretic methods.
Experience or knowledge of reservoir computing, recurrent neural networks, or nature-inspired computing approaches.
Experience or knowledge of applying multi-objective optimisation algorithms or computational simulation.
Experience of working in interdisciplinary research teams or industrial collaborative projects.
Evidence of research publications or presentations at academic conferences.

How To Apply

Applications can be submitted up to 11:55pm (UK time) on Thursday 3rd December 2026.

Interviews are expected to commence week commencing 7 Dec 2026.

Please submit your CV & covering letter via the Heriot-Watt on-line recruitment.

We may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications. We therefore encourage you to submit your application promptly.

We recognise that many candidates use AI tools during the application process and are comfortable with AI being used as a supporting aid. However, we want to hear from you, not AI.

Your application should be an authentic representation of your skills, experience and achievements. Applications that appear to have been fully generated by AI may not accurately reflect your suitability for the role and are therefore discouraged.

At interview, candidates will be expected to discuss and provide evidence of the experience, skills and examples included in their application.

We welcome and will consider flexible working patterns e.g., part-time working and job share options.

Heriot-Watt University is committed to securing equality of opportunity in employment and to the creation of an environment in which individuals are selected, trained, promoted, appraised, and otherwise treated on the sole basis of their relevant merits and abilities. Equality and diversity are all about maximising potential and creating a culture of inclusion for all.

Heriot-Watt University values diversity across our university community and welcomes applications from all sectors of society, particularly from underrepresented groups. For more information, please see our website https://www.hw.ac.uk/uk/services/equality-diversity.htm and also our award-winning work in Disability Inclusive Science Careers https://disc.hw.ac.uk/ .

Use our total rewards calculator: https://www.hw.ac.uk/about/work/total-rewards-calculator.htm to see the value of benefits provided by Heriot-Watt University.

About The Team

You will join an interdisciplinary team working on the UKRI-funded project “Taking Material Reservoir Computers FARR: Foundations for Adaptation, Resilience and Recovery.” This project brings together researchers from Heriot-Watt, Oxford, Liverpool, Sussex, and Ulster universities with expertise spanning mathematics, computer science, robotics, neuroscience, psychology, and materials engineering. The successful candidate will work closely with researchers in mathematics and computer science at Heriot-Watt, while collaborating with colleagues across the wider project consortium.

You will be based in the School of Mathematical and Computer Sciences at Heriot-Watt University, which comprises the Departments of Mathematics, Computer Science, and Actuarial Mathematics & Statistics. The School has a strong research culture and provides a supportive environment for research collaboration and career development. The School is also home to the Mathematics-Driven Innovate Centre (M-DICE), which provides opportunities to engage with industry and external partners through collaborative research, innovation, and knowledge exchange.

The Department of Mathematics is part of the Maxwell Institute for Mathematical Sciences, a joint research institute bringing together the mathematical research activities at Heriot-Watt University and at the University of Edinburgh. The Department is also a co-founder of the International Centre for Mathematical Sciences (ICMS), which organises international workshops and conferences, attracting leading researchers from around world. Together, these institutions contribute to a vibrant and internationally connected mathematical research community in Edinburgh.

The School of Mathematical and Computer Sciences has an Athena SWAN Silver Award (see https://www.hw.ac.uk/schools/mathematical-computer-sciences/about/athena-swan.htm) and is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive working environment and providing equality of opportunity. We encourage applications from under-represented groups, and we welcome requests for flexible working arrangements, which we endeavour to accommodate whenever possible.

About Heriot-Watt University

At Heriot-Watt we are passionate about our values and look to them to connect our people globally and to help us collaborate and celebrate our success through working together. Our research programmes can deliver real world impact which is achieved through the diversity of our international community and the recognition of creative talent that connects our global team.

Our flourishing community will give you the freedom to challenge and to bring your enterprising mind and to help our partners with solutions that can be applied now and in the future. Join us and Heriot Watt will provide you with a platform to thrive and work in a way that also helps you live your life in balance with well-being and inclusiveness at the heart of our global community.
